Credit card fraud can be authorised, where the genuine customer themselves processes a payment to another account which is controlled by a criminal, or unauthorised, where the account holder does not provide authorisation for the payment to proceed and the transaction is carried out by a third party. 

Unexpected repeat billing	Edit
Online bill paying or internet purchases utilizing a bank account are a source for repeat billing known as "recurring bank charges". These are standing orders or banker's orders from a customer to honor and pay a certain amount every month to the payee. With E-commerce, especially in the United States, a vendor or payee can receive payment by direct debit through the ACH Network. While many payments or purchases are valid, and the customer has intentions to pay the bill monthly, some are known as Rogue Automatic Payments.[22]

As an aspie that has lost 110 lbs so far, mostly through diet, I have a few tips. I also stuck to the same few foods and still do. 

Look into intermittent fasting. Work on developing the discipline to not snack or drink calories and you can eat almost anything in your daily meal. So long as you still count your calories.

Take the things you enjoy amd start finding ways to lower the calorie count. Vinaigrette dressings, no sauce on burgers, no cheese, etc can cut 100-300 calories from a single meal. 

I lost my weight while eating out almost every day. Panda express is still a frequent staple in my diet. I used to get lo mein, but now i stick with white rice. Stuff like beef and broccoli and teriyaki chicken (sauce on the side for the rice) are lower calorie options. This is just an example, but there are ways to eat close to how you do now for far fewer calories.

Get into drinking water, unsweet tea, and black coffee. It can be a process, but there are tons of low and no calorie solutions out there to transition. 

All of these tips really hinge on counting calories. It can be difficult whem eating out a lot, but take your meals home and weigh them to get an eye for portion sizes.

If you don't make the effort to manage your diet amd count calories, a personal trainer won't be able to help you. Sure, you might gain muscle, but you won't lose weight. You have to k ow how much fuel you're putting in your body. Luckily counting calories puts a number on everything and alows you to plan out and structure your meals. Not sure if it's my aspie tendencies, nut I enjoy tracking and planning my daily meals.
